headline: High: Cursor’s broad filesystem/network/MCP access can leak or corrupt shared workspace data when paired with next-ai-draw-io’s broad API-backed document processing.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, and clipboard contents, and next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs/text/images/diagrams via natural-language commands. If Cursor writes attacker-controlled content into shared files, next-ai-draw-io can parse it as instructions. The shared local filesystem bridge makes this plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Cursor and next-ai-draw-io share a workspace directory
IF next-ai-draw-io processes file contents as trusted instructions or prompts
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files
Require provenance labels on imported files
Review prompt-like text before processing
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization/provenance checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and can egress broadly to model providers and MCP servers; next-ai-draw-io also sends content to multiple third-party model APIs. In a shared workspace, sensitive files can flow from Cursor into next-ai-draw-io and then onward to external APIs, creating a realistic exfiltration path in default configurations.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace files
IF next-ai-draw-io sends imported document contents to external model APIs
mitigations: Use separate, non-overlapping workspaces
Block sensitive files from the shared directory
Route one agent to local-only models
Restrict clipboard use for sensitive material
requires-engineering: enforce per-file egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shell commands; next-ai-draw-io can also modify files and call external APIs while handling diagrams and documents. Because Cursor explicitly shares state via the local filesystem, concurrent edits to the same repo or diagram files can overwrite each other or corrupt git state without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or diagram directory
IF neither orchestrator provides file or git locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint file ownership
Pause one agent during commits
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Take manual backups before concurrent edits
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can generate code or file edits that next-ai-draw-io may consume as authoritative input for visualization or document transformation. next-ai-draw-io’s natural-language command flow and broad API access increase the chance that an unverified upstream mistake becomes a downstream action, though the pair is not documented as a direct automation chain.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io consumes Cursor output without a verification step
IF the downstream action is file generation or API-backed transformation
mitigations: Insert a human review step
Require schema validation on handoff files
Compare outputs against source documents
Limit downstream actions to previews
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles source code, open files, clipboard contents, and model-provider API keys, while next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, text, images, and diagrams and can send them to multiple external AI providers. If regulated or confidential data is placed in the shared workspace, differing retention and residency behavior across the two tools can create a compliance mismatch; the profiles do not prove a specific jurisdictional violation, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF either agent’s provider retention or residency differs from the organization’s policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Use approved enterprise model endpoints only
Review retention settings for both tools
Separate confidential and non-confidential projects
requires-engineering: formalize data-processing agreements and residency controls
